questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">If the equation (p<sup>2<\/sup> – 3p + 2)x<sup>2<\/sup> + (p – 1)<sup>2<\/sup>x + (p<sup>2<\/sup> – 4p + 3) = 0 is satisfied for more than two different values of x, then p is equal to -<\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
**Question Explanation:
$ In$ this question we have a quadratic equation where coefficients are involving a parameter p, which have more than two distinct values of x, then we have to find the value of parameter p.
$ $
$ $**Concept:
$ This$ question is based on theory of equation.
$ A$ quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0 will become an identity if it has more than two roots and the required condition is a = b = c = 0
$ $
$ $**Solution:
$ $(p2 – 3p + 2)x2 + (p – 1)2x + (p2 – 4p + 3) = 0
$ Since$ given quadratic equation has more than 2 distinct values of x then it will become an identity.
$ $⇒ Coefficient of x2 = 0 and coefficients of x = 0 and constant term = 0
$ $⇒ p2 – 3p + 2 = 0 and (p – 1)2 = 0 and p2 – 4p + 3 = 0
$ $⇒ (p – 1)(p – 2) = 0 ⇒ p = 1 ⇒ (p – 1)(p – 3) = 0
$ $⇒ p = 1 or 2 ⇒ p = 1 or 3
$ $∴ So
$ $
$ $**Final Answer:
$ The$ correct option is (1). 1
